chunks: The chiefs of his people, who did not believe, said: "He is only a man like you. He wishes to acquire ascendancy over you. If God had willed He would have sent down angels. We never heard this from our elders."
ai.seo_question: Why did the chiefs of Hud's people reject his message based on his humanity?
ai.summary: This passage highlights the core Shia theological critique of aristocratic arrogance, where the 'malā’' (elite chiefs) rejected divine guidance based on human lineage rather than spiritual merit. Their argument that God would have sent angels if the message were true reflects a misunderstanding of the wisdom behind human prophets, a theme frequently explored in Tafsir al-Miṣbāḥ and other Shia exegetical works. The reference to ancestors underscores the traditionalist resistance to new revelation, a pattern seen throughout prophetic histories.
